en., yüksek yoğunlukları nedeniyle özel zor: Dense cargoes present particular challenges. Low stowage factor can concentrate a large mass in a small volume. Loading low in the ship can reduce KG and increase GM, producing a stiff response. Check local tank-top loads, hull strength and the complete approved stability criteria; high GM alone does not establish safety.
en.GHG Rating'in temelindeki EVDI (Existing: RightShip's GHG Rating is a commercial comparison of the design-related efficiency of similar vessels. Its methodology uses EEDI, EEXI or EVDI inputs as applicable; an accepted EEXI can supersede EVDI for an existing ship. EEXI is an IMO technical-efficiency requirement under MARPOL Annex VI. The current GHG Rating uses an A–E scale. Neither statutory EEXI compliance nor the GHG Rating guarantees the other. Check the current RightShip methodology and the vessel's verified EVDI, EEXI and GHG data.
en.SMS statik bir el kitabı değil, bir öğre: The SMS includes continuous improvement. Report non-conformities, accidents and near misses, investigate causes and verify corrective actions. Internal audits and management review assess whether procedures work. The planned maintenance system (PMS) supports equipment reliability. Document control and maritime cyber-risk management also form part of the SMS.
en.GM < 0 → TEHLİKELİ: Gemi stabil değil, a: GM < 0 indicates unstable upright equilibrium. GM = 0 has no positive initial restoring stiffness. GM of 0.15 m is a minimum in specified IMO intact-stability criteria, not a universal pass mark. GM between 0.15 and 0.50 m is not automatically acceptable. GM between 0.50 and 1.50 m is not a universal normal range. GM above 1.50 m does not prove safety. GM requires applicable free-surface corrections. Assess GM with the complete GZ curve, downflooding, strength and operating limits.
en.Baş açısını 30-50° yapın: Assess course and speed using ship-specific heavy-weather guidance and observed response; there is no universal 30–50° heading rule.
en.Baş dalgada yüksek hız slamming, poundin: High speed in head seas can increase slamming, pounding and green-water loading. Assess course and speed using ship-specific guidance, sea room and observed response. Following and quartering seas can create surf-riding and broaching risks; no single wave angle is safest for every ship and loading condition.
en.Kıç omuzluktan 22.5°'den daha geriden ya: A vessel coming up from a direction more than 22.5° abaft the beam of the vessel being overtaken.
en.Rüzgâr sancak kıç omuzlukta tutulur; rüz: In the Northern Hemisphere navigable semicircle, traditional guidance places the wind on the starboard quarter while moving safely away from the cyclone track. Use current forecasts, storm movement, sea room and ship limitations; do not follow a fixed heading rule blindly.
en.Rüzgârı sancak baş omuzlukta tutmalı: For the Northern Hemisphere dangerous semicircle: wind on the starboard bow, interpreted with the forecast, sea room and ship limitations.
en.Rüzgârı sancak kıç omuzlukta tutup uzakl: For the Northern Hemisphere navigable semicircle: wind on the starboard quarter while increasing separation safely.
en.Tehlikeli yarım dairede rüzgâr sancak ba: Traditional Northern Hemisphere guidance uses the starboard bow in the dangerous semicircle and the starboard quarter in the navigable semicircle. Consider hemisphere, cyclone track, sea room and vessel response; this is not a universal manoeuvring instruction.
en.Yaklaşık 14 s periyotlu swell kıç omuzlu: Swell of about 14 s period approaches from the quarter (approximately 135° relative). Roll amplitudes increase and the natural roll period approaches the wave encounter period. What is the principal risk?
en.Bayrak devletine veya RO'ya raporlanan D: DCS data reported to the flag state or RO are anonymized by IMO and published in an aggregated form in the IMO GISIS database; Although anonymization hides the identity of the individual ship, it allows the creation of comparative performance tables across the industry by ship type, size and age categories. This global transparency has enabled DCS to transform from a mere regulatory obligation into a commercial pressure tool: charterers and cargo owners are questioning DCS-based efficiency indicators (CII rating, AER trends) when choosing ships to charter, preferring low carbon intensity among similar ships, and some large cargo owners are imposing a minimum CII rating requirement in their contracts. Thus, a ship's DCS data has turned into a performance card that plays a role not only in flag state control but also in its ability to earn freight in the free market; Poor data quality or low ratings are also commercially costly.
en.İkinci Nesil Sağlam Stabilite Kriterleri: The Second Generation Intact Stability Criteria (SGISC) are IMO interim guidelines for assessing dynamic stability failure modes in waves. They supplement the established framework and are not universally mandatory for every ship.
en.Kaptanın gemiye özel talimatları her zam: Call the Master as required by standing orders and whenever the officer of the watch is in doubt: reduced visibility, collision risk or CPA/TCPA concerns, uncertain position, passage-plan difficulties, unexpected depth, steering or propulsion failure, worsening weather, suspected anchor dragging, doubtful pilot or VTS instructions, or distress messages. Calling the Master does not remove the duty to take immediate safety action.
en.Deviation geminin demir kütlesinden kayn: Compass deviation results from the ship's magnetic influences and varies with heading and condition. Use the applicable deviation information and verify compass errors as required.
en.EEXI uyumu, hesapları ve uygulanan kısıt: EEXI compliance under MARPOL Annex VI is documented by the approved EEXI Technical File and the International Energy Efficiency (IEE) Certificate. The initial verification was linked to a specified IAPP periodical survey, but IAPP covers air-pollution certification. Approved EPL or SHAPOLI arrangements govern power reserve, reporting and records. EEXI non-compliance requires action with the Administration or RO and may attract PSC action. EEXI measures technical efficiency; CII addresses annual operational carbon intensity.
en.RPM, exhaust temp, LO basınç, jacket coo: Monitor RPM, exhaust temperature, LO pressure, jacket-cooling temperature and scavenge-air temperature against the operating condition and maker's limits.
Record engine RPM, exhaust temperature, LO pressure, jacket-cooling temperature, turbocharger RPM and fuel pressure with the operating condition needed to interpret them.
en.CSS Code'un Ek 13 hesaplama yöntemi, gem: The Annex 13 calculation method of the CSS Code is based on numerically estimating the inertial force that ship motion exerts on the load. When the ship rolls and pitches at sea, every point on the deck is subjected to an angular acceleration and a corresponding linear acceleration; This acceleration is multiplied by the weight of the load at that point to obtain horizontal and vertical inertia forces, and the net force trying to shift or topple the load is calculated in this way. The most critical parameter of the calculation is the ship's metacentric height (GM): a ship with a high GM behaves 'stiff', that is, completes the roll quickly and with large angular acceleration, which magnifies the inertial forces on the deck load; A 'soft' (tender) ship with a low GM will make slower and larger rolls, the acceleration will be smaller, but an extremely low GM is dangerous in terms of stability. Therefore, lashing design must take into calculation the GM range of the ship in expected loading situations; The same load and the same lashing arrangement may have different safety margins at different GM values. Annex 13 formulates this relationship with standard motion coefficients and design wave conditions to produce the minimum cargo securing capacity required for each load position.
en.Genel yük, proje yükü, çelik ve konteyne: General cargo, project cargo, steel products and containers need securing against forces from ship motions. Apply the approved Cargo Securing Manual and applicable IMO CSS Code or cargo-specific requirements. Geometry, rated capacity, friction and securing-point condition affect the arrangement; adding restraints alone does not establish safety.
en.Madde 9, ISM'i bir öğrenme sistemine dön: ISM Code section 9 requires reporting and analysis of non-conformities, accidents and hazardous occurrences and corrective actions to prevent recurrence. Investigate causes, assign responsibility and verify effectiveness. Closing a report alone does not prove the risk is controlled.
en.Tehlikeli yarım dairede bulunan gemi, rü: Traditional Northern Hemisphere cyclone guidance uses the starboard bow in the dangerous semicircle and the starboard quarter in the navigable semicircle. Reverse the side convention for the Southern Hemisphere. Actual decisions require current forecasts, storm movement, sea room and ship-specific heavy-weather limits.

en.GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safe: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) supports distress alerting, search-and-rescue coordination, maritime safety information and other required communications. GMDSS equipment requirements depend on the sea areas, approved satellite-service coverage and applicable SOLAS requirements.

en.DR dış etkisiz hesap mevkidir; EP dış et: Dead reckoning (DR) advances a previous position using course steered and distance through the water. An estimated position (EP) also allows for estimated current and leeway. Neither replaces an independently established fix.
en.Kodun teknik özü, tahıl kaymasından doğa: The technical essence of the code is to calculate the heeling moment resulting from grain shifting and prove that the ship's stability reserve is sufficient against this. There are certain numerical thresholds: the angle of heel resulting from shearing must not exceed a certain limit (about 12° or the angle of entry of the deck edge into the water, whichever is smaller) and the remaining dynamic stability area must not fall below a minimum value (0.075 m·rad). The calculation is made with different space assumptions for partially filled and fully filled cargo holds. The ship must carry an approved grain loading booklet containing these calculation and a Document of Authorization showing grain transportation competence.
en.Kuralın yetersiz kaldığı durumlar: (a) G: Cases where the rule fails: (a) Tidal period other than six hours: in some areas the HW–LW interval is 5 hours or 7–8 hours; The 6-hour rates of the rule give incorrect results in these ports. (b) Asymmetric tidal profile: in some ports the rising tide may be fast and the falling tide slow (or vice versa); The rule of 12 cannot capture this asymmetry. (c) Critical UKC calculation: the rule of 12 is not sufficient in calculation with narrow safety margins; tidal curve should be used.
en.Onay aşamasında: kaptan stabilite hesapl: At the approval stage: the master must have reviewed and approved the stability calculations; the calculation document must be signed; documents must have been filed.
en.Title 1 ve 2, istihdam ilişkisinin temel: MLC Titles 1 and 2 cover minimum requirements for work on ships and employment conditions. A seafarer's employment agreement (SEA) records agreed pay and duties. Check the SEA, collective agreement and flag implementation. Rest requirements also interact with STCW provisions for watchkeeping personnel.

en., yükleme operasyonlarının ayna görüntüs: Although it may seem like a mirror image of loading operations, it carries additional risks. During unloading, the ship's displacement decreases; Therefore, the KM value changes and GM may decrease unexpectedly. Additionally, adequate propeller immersion must be ensured, minimum draft requirements must be met and trim control must be maintained. Discharging too quickly, unbalanced discharging and delayed ballast removal are the most common hazards.
en.Regulation 20 – Double hull tankers: A d: MARPOL Annex I regulations 19 and 20 address double-hull requirements and phase-out arrangements for applicable oil tankers. Ship size, construction date and the detailed provisions determine applicability; one DWT threshold is not a complete compliance test.
en.Halat işçiliği, gemiciliğin temelidir. D: Ropework is the foundation of seamanship. The right choice of rope, the right knot and the right splice determine both operational efficiency and the safety of life. The rope's material, strength and maintenance play a critical role in mooring, towing and cargo operations.

Consider hemisphere, cyclone track, sea room and vessel response; this is not a universal manoeuvring instruction.

pt.Tehlikeli yarım dairede bulunan gemi, rü: Traditional Northern Hemisphere cyclone guidance uses the starboard bow in the dangerous semicircle and the starboard quarter in the navigable semicircle. Reverse the side convention for the Southern Hemisphere. Actual decisions require current forecasts, storm movement, sea room and ship-specific heavy-weather limits.

Northern Hemisphere cyclone guidance uses the starboard bow in the dangerous semicircle and the starboard quarter in the navigable semicircle. Interpret this with the forecast track, storm movement, sea room and vessel response. The Southern Hemisphere reverses the side convention.

nl.Baş dalgada yüksek hız slamming, poundin: High speed in head seas can increase slamming, pounding and green-water loading. Assess course and speed using ship-specific guidance, sea room and observed response. Following and quartering seas can create surf-riding and broaching risks; no single wave angle is safest for every ship and loading condition.
nl.Rüzgâr sancak kıç omuzlukta tutulur; rüz: In the Northern Hemisphere navigable semicircle, traditional guidance places the wind on the starboard quarter while moving safely away from the cyclone track. Use current forecasts, storm movement, sea room and ship limitations; do not follow a fixed heading rule blindly.
nl.Rüzgârı sancak baş omuzlukta tutmalı: For the Northern Hemisphere dangerous semicircle: wind on the starboard bow, interpreted with the forecast, sea room and ship limitations.
nl.Rüzgârı sancak kıç omuzlukta tutup uzakl: For the Northern Hemisphere navigable semicircle: wind on the starboard quarter while increasing separation safely.

nl.DR dış etkisiz hesap mevkidir; EP dış et: Dead reckoning (DR) advances a previous position using course steered and distance through the water. An estimated position (EP) also allows for estimated current and leeway. Neither replaces an independently established fix.
nl.Kodun teknik özü, tahıl kaymasından doğa: The technical essence of the code is to calculate the heeling moment resulting from grain shifting and prove that the ship's stability reserve is sufficient against this. There are certain numerical thresholds: the angle of heel resulting from shearing must not exceed a certain limit (about 12° or the angle of entry of the deck edge into the water, whichever is smaller) and the remaining dynamic stability area must not fall below a minimum value (0.075 m·rad). The calculation is made with different space assumptions for partially filled and fully filled cargo holds. The ship must carry an approved grain loading booklet containing these calculation and a Document of Authorization showing grain transportation competence.
nl.Kuralın yetersiz kaldığı durumlar: (a) G: Cases where the rule fails: (a) Tidal period other than six hours: in some areas the HW–LW interval is 5 hours or 7–8 hours; The 6-hour rates of the rule give incorrect results in these ports. (b) Asymmetric tidal profile: in some ports the rising tide may be fast and the falling tide slow (or vice versa); The rule of 12 cannot capture this asymmetry. (c) Critical UKC calculation: the rule of 12 is not sufficient in calculation with narrow safety margins; tidal curve should be used.
nl.Onay aşamasında: kaptan stabilite hesapl: At the approval stage: the master must have reviewed and approved the stability calculations; the calculation document must be signed; documents must have been filed.
nl.Title 1 ve 2, istihdam ilişkisinin temel: MLC Titles 1 and 2 cover minimum requirements for work on ships and employment conditions. A seafarer's employment agreement (SEA) records agreed pay and duties. Check the SEA, collective agreement and flag implementation. Rest requirements also interact with STCW provisions for watchkeeping personnel.

ru.İkinci Nesil Sağlam Stabilite Kriterleri: The Second Generation Intact Stability Criteria (SGISC) are IMO interim guidelines for assessing dynamic stability failure modes in waves. They supplement the established framework and are not universally mandatory for every ship.
ru.EEXI uyumu, hesapları ve uygulanan kısıt: EEXI compliance under MARPOL Annex VI is documented by the approved EEXI Technical File and the International Energy Efficiency (IEE) Certificate. The initial verification was linked to a specified IAPP periodical survey, but IAPP covers air-pollution certification. Approved EPL or SHAPOLI arrangements govern power reserve, reporting and records. EEXI non-compliance requires action with the Administration or RO and may attract PSC action. EEXI measures technical efficiency; CII addresses annual operational carbon intensity.
ru.CSS Code'un Ek 13 hesaplama yöntemi, gem: The Annex 13 calculation method of the CSS Code is based on numerically estimating the inertial force that ship motion exerts on the load. When the ship rolls and pitches at sea, every point on the deck is subjected to an angular acceleration and a corresponding linear acceleration; This acceleration is multiplied by the weight of the load at that point to obtain horizontal and vertical inertia forces, and the net force trying to shift or topple the load is calculated in this way. The most critical parameter of the calculation is the ship's metacentric height (GM): a ship with a high GM behaves 'stiff', that is, completes the roll quickly and with large angular acceleration, which magnifies the inertial forces on the deck load; A 'soft' (tender) ship with a low GM will make slower and larger rolls, the acceleration will be smaller, but an extremely low GM is dangerous in terms of stability. Therefore, lashing design must take into calculation the GM range of the ship in expected loading situations; The same load and the same lashing arrangement may have different safety margins at different GM values. Annex 13 formulates this relationship with standard motion coefficients and design wave conditions to produce the minimum cargo securing capacity required for each load position.
ru.Genel yük, proje yükü, çelik ve konteyne: General cargo, project cargo, steel products and containers need securing against forces from ship motions. Apply the approved Cargo Securing Manual and applicable IMO CSS Code or cargo-specific requirements. Geometry, rated capacity, friction and securing-point condition affect the arrangement; adding restraints alone does not establish safety.
ru., yükleme operasyonlarının ayna görüntüs: Although it may seem like a mirror image of loading operations, it carries additional risks. During unloading, the ship's displacement decreases; Therefore, the KM value changes and GM may decrease unexpectedly. Additionally, adequate propeller immersion must be ensured, minimum draft requirements must be met and trim control must be maintained. Discharging too quickly, unbalanced discharging and delayed ballast removal are the most common hazards.
ru.Regulation 20 – Double hull tankers: A d: MARPOL Annex I regulations 19 and 20 address double-hull requirements and phase-out arrangements for applicable oil tankers. Ship size, construction date and the detailed provisions determine applicability; one DWT threshold is not a complete compliance test.

ja.GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safe: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) supports distress alerting, search-and-rescue coordination, maritime safety information and other required communications. GMDSS equipment requirements depend on the sea areas, approved satellite-service coverage and applicable SOLAS requirements.
